basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 25.' and it opens 'Vers. 25. Erat uterque nudus, et non erubescebant. Quae causa erubescentiae esset in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 25. Erat uterque nudus, et non erubescebant. Quae causa erubescentiae esset in illis quos nullus motus inhonestus, nulla carnis titillatio agebat? Nisi enim homo peccasset, nunquam voluptatis ardore | instigaretur. Sed sicut nos oculum hac illae sine laesione aliqua vel petulantia volvimus, vel sicut digitum protendimus, ita membris genitalibus non ad delectationem, sed ad gignendam prolem uteremur. Bene ergo dicitur: Non erubescebant quod nudi essent, qui melius veste innocentiae et immortalitatis jucunditate vestiebantur.
